thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: realtime SLO alert: p99 latency for /v1/chat/streaming > 1.2s (current 1.8s) in us-east-1. Detected 2026-03-15T20:41:17Z. Auto-page oncall.

jin-oncall: I'm on it, paging runtime and SRE. Quick checks first — are there any recent deploys or config changes?

alex-sre: seeing a big tail on streaming write latency. p95 ~ 300ms, p99 ~ 1.8s, long tail up to 9s for chunk writes. Queue depth on streaming-workers has jumped from 30->260 in 5m.

paul-runtime: checking node health and KV cache. `kubectl get pods -l app=streaming -o wide` shows several pods in `Ready` but high CPU. Redis cluster reports evictions and high mem usage. Running `redis-cli --stat` shows spikes.

maria-eng: no user-facing deploys in last 24h from product team. Deploy-bot shows a canary to runtime yesterday 19:30 but no rollout.

ops-bot: autoscaler note: target CPU threshold 70%, current 94% so scale-up blocked by max-replicas cap (10). Provisioning lag ~ 40s due to spot pool pop.

jin-oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) route streaming traffic to dedicated pool (lower concurrency), 2) enable degraded streaming (switch to non-chunking / single-response), 3) throttle bursty clients by rate-limit. Which is fastest?

paul-runtime: I can flip route to dedicated pool now. Command:```shell
redwood route set --prefix /v1/chat/streaming --pool dedicated-us-east-b --drain 30s
```Applying that. Also will start rolling restart of `streaming-nodes` group to drain stuck connections.

alex-sre: while route flip happens, we should clear KV cache shards with high cardinality — `redis-cli -c SHARDSTATS` shows shard-7 at 98% mem. Flushing will reduce pressure but may spike CPU, proceed carefully.

paul-runtime: route change accepted, traffic shifting. logs: `INFO route-change accepted for /v1/chat/streaming -> dedicated-us-east-b (drain 30s)`. Starting rolling restart (grp streaming-nodes, batch 2).

jin-oncall: monitoring synthetic p99 against a canary probe — run once per 5s.

ops-bot: autoscaler cap adjusted from 10->14 (temp) by infra policy to allow scale.

alex-sre: after reroute, synthetic tests show p99 down to ~0.9s within 90s. Real traffic p99 trending down too but still noisy.

maria-eng: quick customer-impact calc: in last 10m ~3.1% of total requests hit p99 > 1.2s, primarily /v1/chat/streaming. Top caller IDs are mobile app builds (80%) and 3 enterprise tenants.

emma-cs: I'm drafting a short notice to affected customers, will include ETA and mitigation steps. cc @liz-product for wording.

liz-product: keep it factual, say we observed intermittent streaming latency and we've rerouted traffic and are running mitigations. Avoid overpromising.

paul-runtime: rolling restart finished for first two batches; logs show some clients had connections reset — expected. Redis shard flush scheduled after next batch.

alex-sre: noticed increased syscall waits on worker processes during high write: `strace` sample shows slow disk write on checkpoint path — investigating if checkpointing frequency combined with KV eviction caused stall.

jin-oncall: action list so far: reroute -> dedicated pool (done), increase autoscale cap (done), rolling restart (in-progress), schedule controlled KV shard flush (planned), enable degraded streaming fallback if p99 rebounds.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: mitigation change recorded in incident timeline, incident id INC-2026-0315-01.

paul-runtime: flushed shard-7 with `redis-cli -c FLUSHDB` on that shard during low traffic window, CPU spike observed but memory reclaimed and evictions dropped to zero.

alex-sre: after flush and restarts, p99 normalized to ~0.95s over last 3m. Tail spikes now rare.

maria-eng: customer impact summary to attach to incident: time window 20:40-20:56 UTC, peak p99 1.8s at 20:41, affected ~3.1% of requests, primary region us-east-1, mitigation applied 20:42 route shift, full recovery to stable p99 by 20:56.

emma-cs: message to customers sent. No escalations from enterprise tenants yet.

jin-oncall: deciding severity: SLO breached but limited user impact and mitigation was effective -> set Sev2. Handoff: I'm handing this to night oncall @lee-oncall with summary + checklist.

lee-oncall: taking handoff. Summary received, will monitor for 2h and keep incident open until we've validated autoscale behavior and removed risky shard flush from next deploy. Anything I should watch immediately?

paul-runtime: watch p99, queue depth, redis evictions, and the autoscaler metrics. Checklist I left in incident doc: `-- verify route permanence if needed`, `-- observe restart logs for OOMs`, `-- coordinate with infra to lock max-replica change if required`.

jin-oncall: thanks — I'll annotate the incident with runbook steps and close once lee confirms stable for 1 hour. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: :clipboard: incident updated: severity=SEV2, owner=jin-oncall, current_assignee=lee-oncall, status=mitigated (monitoring).
